comments.value: I just want to verify. Will UV Tile Discard still be a thing as said in this forum post by a team member? And will the Standard Lite and Toon Standard shader optionally support it? I would love to have more control over my fallback shader, and I rely on UV Tile Discard way too much. Typically the only downside to using it over hiding with blendshapes is that the effect doesn't work with fallback shaders. https://ask.vrchat.com/t/developer-update-13-february-2025/41299/25
This is amazing, always looking at better optimisation for my base. Love the atlasing and mesh combining!
Really interesting! Hope it functions similarly to Polytool and whatnot!

> Will UV Tile Discard still be a thing 

Yes. Custom shader authors can implement support for the avatar optimizer. If the shader is not supported, the avatar optimizer will skip those shaders.

> And will the Standard Lite and Toon Standard shader optionally support [UV tile discard]? 

Our built-in shaders currently do not support UV tile discard - feel free to post a new feature request!

> Our built-in shaders currently do not support UV tile discard - feel free to post a new feature request!

- [Add UV Discarding to Quest Shaders](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/add-uv-discarding-to-quest-shaders) (April 26, 2023) - Tracked

- [UV Tile Discard for Quest Shaders](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/uv-tile-discard-for-quest-shaders) (April 9, 2023)

if the compatibility for the optimizer is added to a shader will it be a simple include cignic, that allows the shader to still function? 

I try to reuse the same functions and textures in weird ways to get funny effects working to avoid excessive compute expense but I would love to see how the system works. 

if it allows for abnormal function plugging such as running Udon video texture through a bunch of distortions, turbulent flow calculations, sampling basic edge detections for a starting point of a curve to use as a procedural normal to use for a  shading specular calculation as well as paralax mapped waveforms n such.. Basically will it be able to support the full range of HLSL that works on vrchat? ._.
This is a welcome feature! Is this going to be a one-and-done feature or will it be expanded on over time as features are added or changed?

It would be neat if the optimizer functioned like the one provided by d4rk, allowing merged materials to make use of UV Tile Discard or similar features if they have toggles. This would ideally require UV Tile Discard support within fallback shaders for consistency.
As long as it's not the toothpick torso for avis
@{5f2cba5631807b34c94a38e1|full_name} That's a great idea! It probably won't be in the initial release - and it's not something we can do on Android/iOS, unfortunately.

@{63691297469f06772579fe6f|full_name} Do you think that running `Cutout`-style alpha-clip would benefit performance at all in place of standard `<NaN, NaN, NaN>` vertex-style tile discard for android/ios devices? Also, do you think cutout style shaders would be possible to have on those platforms (for avatars), since they are rendered along opaque objects, or is the performance cost too substantial on those mobile devices for those to be an option?

@{5f2cba5631807b34c94a38e1|full_name} I'm no shader expert - someone else can probably answer this better. But from what I've heard, cutout shaders are much more expensive on mobile GPUs than on desktop GPUs. The rendering cost is not the same as opaque objects.

details:
*(Note: This feature is still in development, so any of the details below might change before the final release.)*

The Avatar Optimizer runs automatically when you build or upload your avatar. It intelligently generates atlas textures and combines meshes and materials to reduce the number of draw calls, improving performance.

- You can configure the optimization settings to preserve certain blend shapes, skip generating atlas textures, or disable the optimizer entirely.

- You can preview optimized Avatars before uploading to check if the optimizations worked correctly.

- At first, only the Standard Lite and Toon Standard shaders will support material merging and texture atlasing.

- If you're a shader developer, our documentation will explain how to make your custom shader compatible with the avatar optimizer.

Once we're ready, our goal is to test the avatar optimizer in a closed beta to collect more data on its usefulness and to inform our next steps.
title: Automatic Avatar Optimization in SDK
